title: Chicken and Dumplings
summary: Bone-in chicken is browned and simmered into a creamy vegetable stew, then topped with soft dumplings that steam on top until fluffy.
equipment: large heavy casserole (28 cm, 5-6 litres) with a tight lid

ingredients.item: bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and drumsticks
fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Brown the chicken
steps.text: Season the chicken with the salt and pepper. Melt half the butter in the casserole over medium-high heat and brown the chicken skin-side down for 6-8 minutes until golden, then lift it out - this step builds flavour and renders some fat into the pot.

steps.title: Soften the vegetables
steps.text: Lower the heat to medium, add the remaining butter, and cook the onion, carrot and celery for 6-8 minutes until softened. Add the garlic for 1 minute.

steps.title: Build the stew
steps.text: Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then slowly whisk in the stock. Add the thyme and bay leaves, return the chicken to the pot, and simmer gently, partly covered, for 30-35 minutes until the thighs reach 80°C (175°F) and are tender.

steps.title: Shred the chicken
steps.text: Lift the chicken out, discard the skin and bones, and shred the meat into large pieces.

steps.title: Finish the stew
steps.text: Stir the cream and peas into the stew, then return the shredded chicken and bring back to a gentle simmer. Taste and adjust the seasoning.

steps.title: Mix the dumplings
steps.text: Whisk together the flour, baking powder, salt and parsley, then stir in the milk and melted butter just until a soft, sticky dough forms - overmixing at this stage will make the dumplings tough rather than light.

steps.title: Steam the dumplings
steps.text: Drop 12 heaped spoonfuls of the dumpling dough onto the simmering stew, spaced apart. Cover tightly and cook on low heat for 15-18 minutes without lifting the lid, since trapped steam is what cooks the tops, until the dumplings are doubled in size, firm, and a skewer comes out clean.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.text: Let the pot rest for 5 minutes before serving so the stew settles slightly.

tips: Mix the dumpling dough only until just combined - overworking it develops the flour's gluten and makes the dumplings dense.
Common mistake: lifting the lid to check on the dumplings while they steam. Trust the time; removing the lid lets steam escape and can leave the tops undercooked.
Browning the chicken skin first, even though the skin is discarded later, builds a deeper flavour base for the stew.
Shred the chicken into fairly large pieces so it doesn't disappear into the stew.
Space the dumplings out when you drop them in, as they expand significantly while steaming.
storage: Keep in the fridge for up to 3 days; dumplings soften on standing but still taste good. Reheat gently on the hob until piping hot throughout (74°C (165°F)); freezing isn't recommended as the dumplings turn gluey. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (1 hour on a day above 32°C (90°F)).
